wins: Nmap reconnaissance successfully enumerated live hosts and identified three TCP services (22, 80, 443) allowing focused follow-up
Captured consistent HTTP headers that revealed application stack for potential exploitation paths
fails: Failed to obtain valid credentials after repeated brute-force attempts on SSH (port 22), limiting lateral movement
Privilege escalation attempts stalled due to strong syscall restrictions on target host
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance delivered high-quality targeting data, but brute-force credential gathering and privilege escalation remain blocked, preventing mission success.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Password spraying on SSH without context repeatedly returned lockouts and no valid logins

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected
skill_cards.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with nmap scripts

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP service responds with identifiable CMS headers
skill_cards.then_action: Execute targeted nikto scan followed by CMS-specific content discovery

skill_cards.if_condition: When authentication attempts fail repeatedly on SSH
skill_cards.then_action: Switch to low-noise credential profiling via harvester and Burp suite inbound capture

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in reconnaissance phase

next_experiments.title: Shift to passive credential harvesting
next_experiments.description: Deploy harvester-focused reconnaissance and monitor for exposed credentials instead of noisy brute-force attempts on SSH to avoid lockouts.

next_experiments.title: Leverage HTTP-based misconfigurations
next_experiments.description: Use CMS-specific fuzzing and directory brute forcing to find exploitable admin panels or outdated plugins on the identified HTTP service.

next_experiments.title: Investigate lateral movement pathways
next_experiments.description: Map accessible SMB/NFS shares from live hosts to find stored credentials or misconfigurations that could facilitate privilege escalation.
